Jones and Pittman’s taxonomy of impression-management strategies would classify this as which overall project?

choices.text: Unconscious Freudian displacement of oral drives onto the interviewer
Strategic self-presentation: selecting behaviors to shape an attributed identity (likable, competent, moral)
Asch conformity to a wrong line length
Mere exposure (Zajonc) to the interviewer’s face as the sole cause of liking

items.explanation: Impression management is the attempt to control attributed identities. Jones and Pittman distinguished ingratiation (liking), self-promotion (competence), exemplification (moral worth), intimidation, and supplication. The applicant’s mix is strategic self-presentation, compatible with Goffman’s broader dramaturgy. Displacement is a defense mechanism, not this taxonomy. Asch is majority influence on a perceptual judgment. Mere exposure is liking from repeated neutral exposure, not a one-shot interview script.

distractor_rationales.A: Psychodynamic displacement is not Jones and Pittman’s strategy list.
distractor_rationales.C: No confederate majority on line lengths is present.
distractor_rationales.D: Mere exposure does not explain flattery and CV displays as tactics.

items.stem: In Ainsworth’s Strange Situation, a 12-month-old plays using the parent as a base, cries at separation, and is readily comforted at reunion, then returns to play. This pattern is which attachment classification?

choices.text: Insecure-avoidant (Type A): little distress, avoidance at reunion
Insecure-resistant/ambivalent (Type C): distress not soothed, angry clinging
Secure (Type B)
Disorganized (Main and Solomon): freeze/collapse as the only possible secure pattern

items.explanation: Ainsworth’s secure infants use the caregiver as a secure base, protest separation, and settle at reunion. Avoidant infants show muted distress and avoid contact on return. Resistant/ambivalent infants are distressed and not easily soothed, often with anger. Disorganized infants show contradictory or freezing behavior and were added later by Main and Solomon; they are not the secure pattern. Bowlby’s attachment theory supplies the evolutionary-ethological frame for why a secure base matters.

distractor_rationales.A: Avoidant reunion behavior is avoidance, not ready comfort and return to play.
distractor_rationales.B: Resistant infants do not soothe readily; the stem’s child does.
distractor_rationales.D: Disorganized is not the definition of secure attachment.

items.stem: A ground squirrel is more likely to give a predator alarm when nearby listeners are close female kin than when they are unrelated. Hamilton’s rule is offered as the explanation. Which inequality, and which concept, is being invoked?

choices.text: Trivers’s reciprocal altruism, which requires the named sisters to repay the alarm next week as a contract
Wynne-Edwards group selection as the MCAT-preferred substitute for relatedness
Harlow’s contact comfort, because cloth mothers alarm-call
rB > C: inclusive fitness/kin selection can favor a costly alarm when relatedness times benefit to recipients exceeds the cost to the caller

items.explanation: Hamilton’s inclusive-fitness rule says a social behavior is favored when rB > C: relatedness times the benefit to recipients exceeds the actor’s cost. Alarm calling that tracks kinship is a classic illustration. Reciprocal altruism (Trivers) can explain aid among nonkin given later repayment, which the stem does not require. Naive group-selection accounts are not the standard MCAT mechanism here. Harlow showed infants prefer cloth comfort to a wire feeder; that is attachment, not kin-selected alarms.

distractor_rationales.A: The stem varies relatedness, not a repayment contract.
distractor_rationales.B: MCAT-level evolutionary social behavior uses inclusive fitness, not Wynne-Edwards as the preferred engine.
distractor_rationales.C: Harlow’s surrogate mothers are a different literature.

items.stem: A landlord privately endorses hostile stereotypes about a tenant group (prejudice) but, fearing a fair-housing suit, rents to the first qualified applicant. Merton’s typology of prejudice and discrimination would call this person which type?

choices.text: A timid bigot (prejudiced non-discriminator), whose behavior does not match the negative attitude
An all-weather bigot, who both hates and discriminates
An all-weather liberal, who has neither prejudice nor discrimination
A fair-weather liberal, who is unprejudiced but discriminates under social pressure

items.explanation: Prejudice is an attitude (often with affective and cognitive components); discrimination is unequal treatment. They can dissociate. Merton’s timid bigot holds the prejudice but does not discriminate when situational costs are high—the lawsuit-fearing landlord. The all-weather bigot would also refuse to rent. The all-weather liberal has neither. The fair-weather liberal discriminates despite lacking prejudice, under pressure. The stem is attitude without the behavior.

distractor_rationales.B: An all-weather bigot would act on the hostility, not comply with fair housing.
distractor_rationales.C: Hostile stereotypes mean prejudice is present.
distractor_rationales.D: A fair-weather liberal lacks prejudice and still discriminates; this landlord has prejudice and does not discriminate.

items.stem: A hospital scheduling algorithm shortens appointment slots for ZIP codes that historically overlap with redlined districts, with no individual clerk expressing hostility. Outcome data show longer waits for Black patients. This pattern is best labeled how?

choices.text: Individual discrimination only, because an algorithm cannot be institutional
Institutional discrimination: organizational rules or routines producing systematic unequal treatment, even without a bigoted actor at the desk
Prejudice without discrimination, because no clerk used a slur
Goffman stigma only, which is defined as a ZIP-code variable

items.explanation: Institutional (structural) discrimination is unequal outcomes built into policies, algorithms, or standard operating procedures, and it does not require a prejudiced individual at the moment of action. Individual discrimination is a particular person treating another unequally. The algorithm produces extra wait—discrimination in behavior/outcome—not a mere private attitude. Goffman’s stigma is interactional identity spoilage, not a geocoded slot-length rule. Carmichael and Hamilton’s discussion of institutional racism is the usual MCAT contrast with individual bias.

distractor_rationales.A: Institutions can discriminate through routines and code; a smiling clerk is not required.
distractor_rationales.C: Unequal waits are discriminatory outcomes, not prejudice-only.
distractor_rationales.D: Stigma is not defined as a ZIP-code scheduler.

items.stem: Researchers studying a teaching hospital ask how chaplaincy, billing, and the residency each contribute to the equilibrium of the whole organization and to social order, analogizing to organs in a body. Which theoretical approach, associated with Durkheim and later Parsons, is this?

choices.text: Conflict theory in the Marxian sense, emphasizing surplus extraction by a bourgeois board
Symbolic interactionism (Blumer), which refuses any analysis above a dyad’s gestures
Structural functionalism: institutions are analyzed by the functions they perform for system stability
Rational-choice theory, which treats the hospital as a single utility-maximizing shopper

items.explanation: Functionalism, from Durkheim’s social facts and organic solidarity through Parsons’s AGIL systems, analyzes institutions by the functions they serve for cohesion and equilibrium—the organ analogy is textbook. Marxian conflict theory would ask which class benefits and how contradictions drive change. Symbolic interactionism (Mead/Blumer) inspects meaning in face-to-face interaction, not system organs. Rational choice models individual utility, not a hospital-as-organism metaphor.

distractor_rationales.A: A board extracting surplus is conflict analysis, not the equilibrium-organ frame.
distractor_rationales.B: Blumer’s premises are about meaning, not societal organs.
distractor_rationales.D: A utility-maximizing shopper is not Durkheim’s functional analysis.

items.stem: An ethnographer sits in a diabetes clinic and records how “compliance” is negotiated turn by turn: what a glucometer reading is taken to mean, how a missed dose is excused, how identities of “good patient” are performed. Which pair of approaches is most tightly fitted to this micro-meaning project?

choices.text: Marxist conflict theory, because only class fractions can speak in a clinic
Durkheimian functionalism, because the ethnographer is measuring organic solidarity with a dynamometer
Feminist theory only if no men are present, which is its defining axiom
Symbolic interactionism (Mead, Blumer) and social constructionism (Berger and Luckmann), which treat meanings and “facts” of illness as produced in interaction and institutionalization

items.explanation: Symbolic interactionism holds that people act toward things on the basis of meanings that arise in interaction (Blumer’s premises, from Mead). Social constructionism (Berger and Luckmann) extends that insight: realities, including illness categories, are built and sedimented through social processes. A turn-by-turn clinic study is that program. Conflict theory can study clinics but is not this meaning-negotiation method. Functionalism’s system needs are not measured by dyadic excuses. Feminist theory is not defined by the absence of men.

distractor_rationales.A: Class analysis is not implied merely by recording conversational meaning.
distractor_rationales.B: Organic solidarity is a macrosocial cohesion type, not a dynamometer reading of excuses.
distractor_rationales.C: Feminist approaches analyze gendered power; they are not “no men in the room.”

items.stem: A patient with influenza stays home from the wards, is not blamed for being ill, is expected to try to get well, and is expected to seek competent medical advice. Parsons’s sick role, as an account of medicine as an institution, includes which pair of rights and obligations?

choices.text: Exemption from normal duties and from blame, plus obligations to want recovery and to seek help
A right to remain ill indefinitely with no obligation to consult a physician
Marx’s claim that medicine exists only to reproduce labor power, which forbids any sick-role rights
The hidden curriculum of K–12 schooling as the definition of the sick role

items.explanation: Parsons modeled the sick role as a patterned, socially controlled deviation: the sick person is exempt from ordinary roles and not held responsible for the condition, but must treat illness as undesirable and cooperate with technically competent healers. That is how medicine as an institution manages illness. Unlimited right to remain ill without help contradicts those obligations. Marxian critiques of medicine are a different theoretical register. The hidden curriculum is a schooling concept (Jackson; Bowles and Gintis), not the sick role.

distractor_rationales.B: Parsons required the obligation to seek help and to want to get well.
distractor_rationales.C: Conflict critiques do not erase Parsons’s named four-part role as the standard MCAT account.
distractor_rationales.D: Hidden curriculum belongs to education, not the influenza sick role.

items.stem: A school rewards sitting still, raising a hand, and deferring to the teacher’s clock more consistently than it rewards unusual scientific curiosity. Bowles and Gintis interpret this hidden curriculum as which institutional function of education?

choices.text: A purely meritocratic filter that Davis and Moore would say is unrelated to class
Correspondence with workplace authority relations, reproducing class structure through schooling as an institution
Weber’s Protestant ethic as the official math syllabus
Parsons’s sick role applied to children who sit still

items.explanation: The hidden curriculum is the unofficial lessons of school (punctuality, obedience, hierarchy). Bowles and Gintis’s correspondence principle claims those lessons mirror capitalist workplace relations and thus contribute to social reproduction. Davis–Moore functionalist meritocracy is the rival story this critique targets. Weber’s Protestant ethic is a thesis about capitalism’s cultural origins, not a math syllabus. The sick role is a medical-institution concept, not a description of classroom docility.

distractor_rationales.A: Bowles and Gintis deny that school is a class-neutral merit sieve.
distractor_rationales.C: The Protestant ethic is not the hidden-curriculum claim.
distractor_rationales.D: Sitting still in class is not Parsons’s influenza role.

items.stem: A hospital deploys a new mRNA platform within months, while consent templates, kinship rules about stored samples, and malpractice doctrine lag by years. Ogburn’s concept that names this gap is which of the following?

choices.text: Culture shock, which is a society-level legal delay rather than an individual’s strain in a new culture
McDonaldization (Ritzer) as a synonym for delayed ethics committees
Cultural lag: material culture (technology) changes faster than nonmaterial culture (norms, laws, meanings)
Assimilation, because lag is defined as English-only signage

items.explanation: Ogburn’s cultural lag is the delay of nonmaterial culture behind material invention—the classic cars-before-traffic-laws example, here mRNA before updated consent and kinship norms. Culture shock is an individual’s disorientation in an unfamiliar culture. Ritzer’s McDonaldization is efficiency, calculability, predictability, and control, not lag per se. Assimilation is absorption of a minority into a dominant culture, not a technology–norm gap.

distractor_rationales.A: Culture shock is not Ogburn’s macrosocial lag of laws behind gadgets.
distractor_rationales.B: McDonaldization is a rationalization thesis, not the name of the delay.
distractor_rationales.D: Assimilation is a different cultural process than material/nonmaterial mismatch.

items.stem: A city closes bilingual clinics and posts English-only wayfinding so that “everyone uses the same system.” Advocates of multiculturalism object. Which contrast is most accurate?

choices.text: The policy is culture shock, a legal term for bilingualism
The policy is a subculture of hospital engineers, which is the definition of assimilation
Sapir–Whorf linguistic determinism requires English-only signs for thought to occur
The policy is assimilation (melting-pot pressure toward a dominant pattern); multiculturalism would maintain legitimate cultural pluralism in institutions

items.explanation: Assimilation is the process of taking on the dominant group’s language and institutions, historically imaged as a melting pot. Multiculturalism (cultural pluralism) values persistence of distinct cultural streams within a shared polity. English-only clinics are assimilationist. Culture shock is individual strain abroad. A subculture is a group with distinct norms inside a larger culture, not the definition of this city policy. Sapir–Whorf concerns language shaping thought, not a requirement for monolingual signage to think.

distractor_rationales.A: Culture shock is not the name of an English-only ordinance.
distractor_rationales.B: Subculture ≠ assimilationist city policy.
distractor_rationales.C: Whorf does not legislate English-only wayfinding as a condition of thought.

items.stem: In a four-stage demographic-transition teaching model, a country’s crude death rate falls from 30 to 12 per 1,000 over two decades while the birth rate remains near 38. Population grows rapidly. Which stage is this, and what typically drives the death-rate drop?

choices.text: Stage 2: mortality falls first (sanitation, nutrition, basic medicine) while fertility stays high
Stage 1: both rates still high, so growth remains near zero
Stage 3: fertility has already fallen to match mortality
Stage 4: both rates are low and the boom is over

items.explanation: In the standard four-stage demographic transition, stage 1 has high birth and death rates. Stage 2 is the mortality decline—public health, food, and infectious-disease control—while fertility remains high, producing explosive growth. Stage 3 is the later fertility decline. Stage 4 is low-low with slower growth. Five-stage variants add a possible stage-5 below-replacement fertility; they do not relocate the first mortality drop out of the early-transition boom described here.

distractor_rationales.B: Stage 1 would not show a collapsed death rate with a still-high birth rate.
distractor_rationales.C: Stage 3 is when births fall, which has not yet happened in the stem.
distractor_rationales.D: Stage 4 is low fertility and low mortality, not a 38 birth rate.

items.stem: Two tenant groups want the same repair ordinance. Group A is furious but has no office, lawyers, or mailing list. Group B is only moderately aggrieved but has a funded staff and ties to a citywide coalition. Resource-mobilization theory (McCarthy and Zald) predicts which outcome, relative to a pure relative-deprivation account (Gurr)?

choices.text: Only Group A can succeed, because anger is necessary and sufficient
Group B is more likely to become an effective social movement, because organization and resources, not grievance intensity alone, convert unrest into action
Wirth’s urbanism thesis forbids any tenant movement in cities
Demographic transition stage 2 will automatically pass the ordinance

items.explanation: Relative deprivation emphasizes felt grievance as the spark of movements. Resource-mobilization theory replies that grievances are common; what varies is money, staff, networks, and organization. A moderately angry but resourced group can outperform a furious unorganized one. Wirth’s urbanism is about city social psychology (blase attitude, segmental roles), not a ban on movements. Demographic transition is a fertility–mortality model, not an ordinance generator.

distractor_rationales.A: Resource mobilization denies that intensity of anger is sufficient.
distractor_rationales.C: Urban sociology does not entail that tenant movements are impossible.
distractor_rationales.D: Stage 2 of the transition is a population-growth phase, not a housing-law mechanism.

items.stem: Two applicants have identical GPAs. The one who can talk museum internships, chamber music, and “concerted cultivation” interview banter (Lareau) is rated more “collegial” on the MMI. Bourdieu would treat that edge as which kind of resource, and to what reproductive effect?

choices.text: Marxian raw labor power only, which is identical to knowing Brahms
Davis–Moore functionalist proof that the rating is a pure scarcity rent for talent
Cultural capital: embodied tastes and institutional credentials that schools and professions reward, reproducing class advantage beyond wages
Weberian party membership in a political machine, which is the only capital Bourdieu named

items.explanation: Bourdieu distinguished economic, social, and cultural capital. Cultural capital (embodied habitus, objectified goods, institutionalized degrees) is converted into advantages in educational and professional fields, a mechanism of social reproduction. Marx’s labor power is not exhausted by high-culture fluency, though conflict theory more broadly cares about class. Davis–Moore would read unequal reward as functional for talent allocation—the view Bourdieu opposes here. Weber’s class/status/party triad is related stratification language, but “cultural capital” is Bourdieu’s term.

distractor_rationales.A: Knowing Brahms is not “labor power” in Marx’s technical sense.
distractor_rationales.B: The identical-GPA design is meant to show a non-merit, class-cultured bonus.
distractor_rationales.D: Bourdieu named cultural (and social, economic) capital, not only party.

items.stem: Marmot’s Whitehall studies found a stepwise gradient in coronary mortality across British civil-service grades, even though all groups had access to the National Health Service. Which conclusion about class and health is most justified?

choices.text: Only the unemployed are unhealthy; employed grades should be identical
Weber denied that status can affect the body, so Whitehall refutes Weber
The gradient proves Davis–Moore meritocracy causes infarctions by justice
A socioeconomic gradient in health can persist above poverty and despite universal access, implicating status, control, and related class-linked conditions—not access alone

items.explanation: The socioeconomic gradient in health is the graded, not binary, association of SES with morbidity and mortality. Whitehall is famous because it appears among employed, NHS-covered civil servants, so “no insurance” and “absolute destitution” cannot be the whole story. Control, hierarchy, and other class-linked exposures are implicated. Weber actually made status a distinct stratification dimension, compatible with a gradient. Davis–Moore does not claim justice of infarcts as functional necessity.

distractor_rationales.A: Whitehall’s point is the gradient among the employed, not a healthy-worker plateau.
distractor_rationales.B: Weber included status and life chances; Whitehall does not refute him.
distractor_rationales.C: Functional meritocracy is not the cardiologic mechanism Marmot described.

items.stem: A rural county has the state’s highest diabetes prevalence and amputation rate and the fewest endocrinologists and diabetes educators per capita. Tudor Hart’s inverse care law names which relationship?

choices.text: The availability of good medical care tends to vary inversely with the need of the population served
Care is always proportional to need in market systems, so the county is a measurement error
Only individual prejudice by named endocrinologists can produce a shortage
Whitehall already proved rurality is protective, contradicting the amputation rate

items.explanation: Hart’s inverse care law (1971) states that good medical care is least available where it is most needed, especially where market forces dominate. High-need, low-supply counties are the illustration. It is an empirical regularity about distribution, not a claim that measurement must be wrong. Institutional and market allocation can produce shortages without a single prejudiced specialist. Whitehall is an occupational-grade gradient in Britain, not a finding that rural high-need areas are protected.

distractor_rationales.B: The law is precisely that need and supply often run opposite, not in proportion.
distractor_rationales.C: Structural maldistribution does not require a named bigoted clinician.
distractor_rationales.D: Whitehall does not cancel rural amputations as a disparity signal.

items.stem: Undocumented patients delay ED care until a surgical emergency. Link and Phelan’s fundamental-cause theory of health disparities would emphasize which point?

choices.text: Once germ theory is known, social position cannot affect infectious risk

SES and socially excluded legal status are flexible resources (money, power, knowledge, beneficial social connections, freedom to choose) that keep reproducing unequal health even as specific diseases and mechanisms change
Only genetic ancestry, not exclusion from insurance, can delay presentation
Parsons’s sick role requires undocumented patients to be blamed for symptoms

items.explanation: Link and Phelan argue that socioeconomic status is a fundamental cause of disease: it commands flexible resources that can be used to avoid risks and minimize consequences no matter which mechanisms are currently salient. Legal exclusion and social exclusion restrict those resources, producing delayed care and worse outcomes. Germ theory did not erase class gradients; mechanisms were replaced. Genetics does not exhaust presentation delay when insurance and deportation fear operate. Parsons’s sick role is a functionalist ideal, not a requirement to blame excluded patients.

distractor_rationales.A: Fundamental-cause theory exists because gradients survive mechanism change, including after germ theory.
distractor_rationales.C: Access barriers are exactly the sort of resource restriction the theory highlights.
distractor_rationales.D: The sick role’s “not responsible” clause is not a license to blame undocumented patients.
